feasibility: Pure calendar arithmetic over naive datetimes; a compact core that is fully testable within one run
problem: Standard five-field cron expressions are easy to get wrong and hard to read; validation errors are terse, the day-of-month/day-of-week rule surprises even experienced operators, and no zero-dependency Python library both explains and computes schedules.
reason: Highest weighted total; combines three fragmented capabilities behind one small dependency-free interface
target_user: Developers and operators embedding cron schedules in applications, dashboards, CI configuration, and internal tooling
title: Cronplain
why_now: Cron syntax now appears far beyond Unix crontab in job runners and CI platforms, while supply-chain review pressure such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act makes zero-dependency libraries genuinely attractive

problem: Environment files drift from their example templates and hide duplicate keys, quoting mistakes, and missing variables until runtime.
reason: Existing linting setups already catch most of these classes of mistakes
target_user: Teams keeping deployment configuration in .env files under version control
title: Envcheck
why_now: Twelve-factor configuration remains the default for containerized services

feasibility: Core checks are compact, but correctness hinges on real filesystem behavior
problem: User-supplied paths reach file operations without a systematic check for traversal, absolute escapes, or platform quirks.
reason: Highest-risk cases need real filesystem semantics beyond a first release
target_user: Reviewers and authors of services that accept file paths from untrusted input
title: Pathguard
why_now: Path handling bugs remain a recurring class of security advisories

feasibility: Small, easily tested operations over line-oriented input
problem: JSONL data plumbing needs deterministic validate, sort, dedup, split, and merge operations without pulling a full query engine.
reason: General-purpose tools already cover nearly all of these operations
target_user: Engineers moving line-delimited JSON between systems
title: Jsonlkit
why_now: JSONL is the default exchange format for log and event pipelines

feasibility: Doable, but negation, directory-only, and glob-star rules interact in tricky ways
problem: Tools that stage or package files need to evaluate ignore rules without shelling out to git, and the rule semantics are subtle.
reason: Matching semantics are subtle enough that a first release risks wrong answers
target_user: Authors of build, backup, and packaging tools
title: Gitignore matcher
why_now: Independent tooling keeps reimplementing the same matching rules incorrectly

feasibility: Compact parser with a well-defined grammar
problem: Durations written as 1h30m or PT1H30M need lossless conversion to and from seconds across interfaces.
reason: Well-trodden space; a new core adds little beyond existing parsers
target_user: Developers parsing configuration values and command-line options
title: Humanspan
why_now: Interval configuration keeps appearing in schedulers and observability tooling

feasibility: Small validation core over message text
problem: Commit message conventions are checked inconsistently across repositories and continuous integration setups.
reason: Existing hook-based checkers cover most teams already
target_user: Maintainers enforcing commit standards in continuous integration
title: Commit conform
why_now: Conventional commit prefixes remain the dominant convention

feasibility: Moderate parsing effort with limited depth
problem: Markdown tables need lossless conversion to and from CSV or TSV for documentation pipelines.
reason: Shallow core with limited room for meaningful depth
target_user: Technical writers and documentation tool builders
title: Table convert
why_now: Docs-as-code pipelines keep exchanging tabular data

feasibility: Pure in-memory core with a pluggable claim store; deterministic, integer-only, and fully verifiable within one run
problem: Delivery systems retry, so 'apply this callback' is unsafe unless a claim store and the ledger move together; teams hand-roll both and the two drift apart into double credits.
reason: Highest weighted total; fuses the two strongest research signals (retried delivery, balancing) behind one small interface
target_user: Backend engineers building wallets, billing, and payment-adjacent services
title: Ledgerpost
why_now: At-least-once delivery is the norm across payment platforms, while supply-chain review pressure keeps pushing embedded financial code toward zero-dependency libraries

feasibility: Matching core is testable, but tolerance and grouping rules for real flows exceed one verifiable run
problem: Reconciliation tools match one-to-one while real payment flows carry one-to-many settlements, partial refunds, and FX splits.
reason: Strong need, but the rule surface is too large to verify honestly in a first release
target_user: Finance engineering teams matching expected against settled transactions
title: Recmatch
why_now: Surveys keep ranking reconciliation among the costliest manual back-office workflows

problem: Monetary values passed through floats pick up rounding noise that reconciliation cannot absorb.
reason: Well-trodden space; a standalone type adds less than folding it into a posting engine
target_user: Developers representing amounts in service boundaries
title: Minormoney
why_now: Minor-unit representation keeps resurfacing as the fix in financial engineering handbooks

problem: Every retrying integration rebuilds an atomic claim store for idempotency keys.
reason: Narrow slice of the posting-engine problem; delivers more value as part of it
target_user: Authors of integration and webhook handlers
title: Claimkey
why_now: Provider documentation increasingly prescribes idempotency keys while libraries rarely ship the store

feasibility: Full message schemas are too broad for one verifiable release
problem: Payment message files fail validation late, with errors that hide the offending element.
reason: Scope risk: honest coverage of even one message family exceeds the run budget
target_user: Engineers migrating payment message flows to ISO 20022
title: Paincheck
why_now: Migration programs continue to surface tooling gaps

problem: Answering as-of balances and trial balances over posting streams requires ad hoc database queries per team.
reason: Useful only atop a ledger; a natural extension of the selected core instead
title: Ledgerq
why_now: Event-sourced accounting keeps growing in backend stacks

problem: Currency conversion applied without an explicit quote and rounding policy silently loses cents.
reason: Niche scope with shallow depth on its own
title: Fxquote
why_now: Cross-border payment volumes keep FX handling in application code

feasibility: Parser breadth across formats risks unverifiable scope
problem: Each payment provider delivers a different file layout, forcing hours of manual normalization before matching.
reason: Breadth of format coverage cannot be honestly finished and verified in one run
stack: Python with CSV and XML parsing
title: Reconfeed
why_now: Provider format fragmentation is the top reported reconciliation barrier
